nodes_changed.name: init
nodes_changed.signature: pub async fn init(config: DbConfig) -> Result<DbContext, DbError>
nodes_changed.doc:
Opens the database pool and checks the workspace schema is at the

baseline this binary embeds. It runs no DDL (RFD-rwdwbst8, "Migration

and runtime are separate principals"): the migrate step applies the

migrations, as the migration principal, before any workload starts —

the `causeway-migrate` Job in a cluster, `db:migrate` on a developer

host, `TestWorkspace` in tests.



The schema is whatever the connection's `search_path` resolves first.

Every workspace lives in its own `cw_<workspace>` schema and `public`

holds only the extensions, so a connection that resolves to `public` is

one whose workspace schema does not exist: a workspace mid-rebuild, or a

URL that lost its `search_path`. The pool refuses it, and the process

restarts until the schema is back.



# Errors



[`DbError::SchemaNotCurrent`] when a migration this binary embeds is

pending, failed part-way or was applied with other contents. A schema

ahead of the binary, as during a rollout, is current enough: the

migrations it lacks are a newer build's.

nodes_changed.name: startup_accepts_a_migrated_schema_and_refuses_one_behind
nodes_changed.doc:
A workload's startup checks the schema and runs no DDL, because only

the migrate step holds DDL rights (RFD-rwdwbst8): a migrated workspace is current, and one the migrate step has

not finished stops startup naming the migration.

node.signature: fn propose_error(error: causeway_db_core::DbError) -> ConnectError
node.doc:
A proposal the registry refuses. The one refusal a caller can cause is

naming a container the registry does not hold, which the database

reports as a foreign-key violation; that is the caller's argument, not

a precondition, and the message says so instead of quoting the

constraint. Anything else is the store, and reads as unavailable.

node.signature: pub async fn adopt_store_instance( &self, kind: StoreKind, placeholder: &str, instance: &str, display_name: &str, environment: StoreEnvironment, ) -> Result<Uuid, DbError>
node.doc:
Moves a store from a placeholder instance name to the identity the

source reports (RFD-q10sm0wq d13: the metastore, not the workspace).

When the placeholder row exists and the real one does not, the row is

renamed in place so its containers and bindings follow; when the real

row already exists, it is refreshed and a remaining placeholder is

left for the coherence gate to report rather than merged blindly.



# Errors



Returns [`DbError`] when the write fails.

node.name: record_share_grant
node.signature: pub async fn record_share_grant( &self, consumer: &PhysicalContainer, environment: StoreEnvironment, kind: ShareKind, provider: &str, share_name: &str, provider_description: Option<&str>, observed_from: &str, ) -> Result<Uuid, DbError>
node.doc:
Records that `consumer` (a container of kind `share`) is fed by a

share from `provider` (RFD-q10sm0wq d14). Ensures the store and the

container chain exist; an open grant of the same share is refreshed.

Returns the grant id.



# Errors



Returns [`DbError`] when the write fails.

Eight, because a grant is identified by all of them: who consumes
it, in which environment, of what kind, from which provider, under
which name, described how, and observed from where. A parameter
struct here would name the same fields twice.

their ids by column name.



A physical column is a resource of its own, minted on first observation

and never re-minted; a later observation refreshes its description. No

term binding is touched.

Returns an error when the asset is unknown to the catalog or the write

fails.

them by equality. A term the catalog does not know is skipped.



# Errors



Returns the database error when the replacement fails.

node.name: list_dcat_related_entities
node.signature: fn list_dcat_related_entities( &self, roots: &[uuid::Uuid], ) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<uuid::Uuid>, DbError>>;
node.doc:
The DCAT distributions and access services of the given datasets

(RFD-2x49z609 determination 8), roots excluded.



Walks `catalog_semantic_relationships` two hops at most: a dataset's

`distribution` objects, the `access_service` objects of those

distributions, and the `serves_dataset` subjects that serve the

dataset directly. DCAT relations are not lineage and never widen

a derivation walk.

node.name: list_derived_entities
node.signature: fn list_derived_entities( &self, roots: &[uuid::Uuid], ) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<uuid::Uuid>, DbError>>;
node.doc:
Transitive derivation closure of the given entities (RFD-0116).



Walks `data_lineage` downstream from the roots and returns every

reachable catalog entry's id, roots excluded. Every relationship

except `supersedes` propagates: `derives_from`, `enriches`, and

`feeds` all move data downstream, and a governing agreement

follows the data — over-attaching a duty is recoverable,

missing a derived asset under-governs it. `supersedes` is

RFD-0107 revision lineage: both ends are the same asset identity

across a rename, so it carries no derivation.



Traversal is depth-capped rather than cycle-detected; a cycle in

asserted lineage terminates at the cap instead of hanging the

resolver.

Pages bindings whose digest differs from `reference_digest`.

node.name: initialize_catalog_entry_content
node.signature: fn initialize_catalog_entry_content( &self, entity_id: EntityId, now: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, ) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<(), DbError>>;
node.doc:
Creates the content row for a newly discovered object, leaving an

existing one alone.



Discovery knows an object exists; it has measured nothing about it.

Upserting its empty record would publish those blanks over whatever

the sniffer recorded -- `content_meta`, the columns, the extracted

text -- because the upsert assigns every column and a rediscovery

carries a fresh `updated_at`, so the monotonic guard admits it. That

is how every classified entry in a workspace became `(unknown)` and

lost its explorer. Discovery writes only the row's existence.

entry) has no physical columns; that records nothing and returns 0.

node.doc:
Creates a content row if absent, in `schema`.



`DO NOTHING`, not `DO UPDATE`: discovery knows only that the object

exists. The upsert beside this one assigns every column, so running it

with an empty record publishes blanks over whatever the sniffer measured

-- and a rediscovery carries a fresh `updated_at`, which the monotonic

guard admits. Schema-parameterised so the guarantee is testable against a

disposable schema without touching the process environment.

node.doc:
Re-keys the in-memory projection seed onto the durable identities the

ingest pass has already bound (RFD-0107).



The mock seed derives entity ids and URNs from asset names; when a

fixture was renamed under a stable `durable_source_id`, the binding in

`source_identities` still carries the original entity id and URN. This

pass swaps the name-derived identity for the bound one — and keeps the

bound (immutable) slug — so a rename updates the display name without

minting a new identity, and the stale-entity reconcile finds nothing to

tombstone. No-op when the cutover flag is off or nothing diverges.

node.doc:
Hard-deletes every metadata row for the given entities, including the

append-only ledger tables.



This erases governance history. It exists only for resetting

development/test workspaces and must never run against production —

callers are responsible for enforcing that boundary (the seed job

refuses when `CAUSEWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ENV` is `prod`). Prefer

[`tombstone_metadata_rows_for_entities_in_tx`].

Returns [`DbError`] when any of the deletes fail.

node.doc:
Ends the subjects' open stuck-work records as `superseded`, naming the

tombstone as actor and reason, and leaves their payloads in place.



`superseded`, not `succeeded`: the work did not finish, it stopped

applying. A record that had already ended is not touched, and the

number of records closed is returned so a caller can say so.



# Errors



Returns the database error when the update fails.

node.name: tombstone_metadata_rows_for_entities_in_tx
node.signature: pub async fn tombstone_metadata_rows_for_entities_in_tx( tx: &mut Transaction<'_, Postgres>, entity_ids: &[Uuid], entity_urns: &[String], ) -> Result<(), DbError>
node.doc:
Retires the given entities from serving surfaces while preserving the

append-only metadata ledger.



Semantics per table:



* `metadata_domain_events`, `metadata_decisions`, `metadata_observations`,

`manual_actions`, `manual_action_claims` — never touched; they are the

system of record.

* `metadata_claims` — active claims flip to `status = 'retracted'`; rows

are never deleted.

* `entity_identities` — deleted (source-alias resolution rows; the

replacement seed entity re-creates its own aliases).

* dirty-queue tables — deleted (rebuildable work dispatch, keyed by URN).

* `entities` — soft-retired: `status = 'deleted'`, `deleted_at` set, and

the URN/canonical key are moved aside with a deterministic

`::retired::<entity_id>` suffix so the replacement seed entity can

claim the original URN (`entity_urn` and `(entity_kind, canonical_key)`

are unique). Ledger rows keep the original `subject_urn` verbatim.

* `metadata_domain_events` — additionally gains one appended

`entity_retired` event per entity (reason `seed_reconcile`), written

in this transaction with a deterministic idempotency key so re-runs

are no-ops. No supersedes linkage is recorded: durable old→new

identity (RFD-0107) has not landed, so the retirement event carries

only the entity id, URN, and reason.



# Errors



Returns [`DbError`] when a statement fails or a retirement event

cannot be encoded.

node.doc:
Inserts or refreshes one queue row on `executor`, then notifies the

queue's LISTEN channel.



A conflicting pending row is refreshed in place (payload, priority,

reason, availability, lease) rather than dropped: queue idempotency

keys are stable per subject and kind, so `DO NOTHING` would silently

discard a *newer* payload while an older one sits in the queue (the

sniff queue established this refresh pattern). The lease reset re-arms

leased work; downstream processing is idempotent and the catalog

adjunct upserts are monotonic on `updated_at`, so a concurrent

re-claim converges.



Generic over the executor so the same statement serves both the

standalone enqueue and the atomic resolution-output transaction.

node.doc:
Persists one resolution's full output atomically.



Decision, domain events, both outbox rows, and the projection-refresh

queue row commit in one transaction, so a crash can never persist a

decision without its journal events or its catalog refresh. Resolvers

must use this instead of sequencing the singular appends themselves:

their semantic no-op guards skip re-persisting on retry, so a

partially-committed output would never be repaired.

node.doc:
Marks every other active claim of `claim_kind` from `source_system`

on the subject as superseded by `keep`, and returns how many.



A source that re-declares the same fact on every pass (a connector

sync stamps `synchronized_at` into the payload, so each pass is a

new claim) would otherwise leave its history active; the newest

still wins by rank, but the considered set grows without bound.

node.name: upsert_directory
node.signature: pub async fn upsert_directory( pool: &PgPool, declaration: &DirectoryDeclaration, ) -> Result<DirectoryUpsert, DbError>
node.doc:
Writes the declared directory into the workspace's people schema in one

transaction. Rows are upserted by id; display names, short codes, kinds,

ranks, and titles follow the declaration, and a person's profile is

created when it is missing. Nothing is deleted: a handle the manifest

database error that aborted the transaction.

node.doc:
Map a directory row into the domain [`Party`].



The row boundary is where storage strings become types (RFD Phase 1):

- `id` parses strictly through [`PartyRef::parse`] — an ill-formed

handle is surfaced as a [`DbError`], not silently coerced, because

every downstream consumer (chips, click-through URLs, projection

keys) assumes the handle grammar.

- `kind`/`status` parse lossily: the schema CHECK-constrains both to

their two known labels, so an unknown label means a corrupt row and

the display-safe defaults (`person`, `active`) are preferable to

failing the whole read.

node.name: a_persona_token_approves_a_publication_and_the_approval_names_a_party
node.signature: async fn a_persona_token_approves_a_publication_and_the_approval_names_a_party()
node.doc:
The governed write, end to end — the thing this repository could not

do before the persona corpus existed (RFD-ykd2dx4p).



Before this test existed, no integration test anywhere performed a

governed write. The nearest thing reached the authorization boundary

and stopped, and the seed job's fixture approval minted

`user:development-fixture-owner` — real Cedar, an identity no

directory claims. So the two halves of the model were each exercised

alone and never together: Cedar said the action was permitted, the

directory said who could be accountable for it, and nothing ever

asked both questions about the same token.



This asks both. A persona token carries the subject

`person_profile` holds, so the same credential that Cedar permits is

one the directory resolves to a party — and the approval it writes

names that party and carries the real policy bundle's evidence.



Against a workspace the testkit migrates in an ephemeral Postgres

(RFD-fpg4tnq2), with the people directory loaded the way

`causeway-seed --profile people` loads it.

node.doc:
The people directory from `{titles,people,teams}.jsonl` in the

directory of principals the topology names:

titles, people with their titles and identity-provider subjects, and

teams, upserted by handle through the people slice's write port.



This is the `people` loader of the development data RFD; it runs first

so every later steward, owner, party, and product-manager handle

resolves, and it is production-like, so it carries no fixture content.



The record shapes belong to the people component, not to this job

(RFD-ykd2dx4p determination 2): one declaration, read at compile time

by the component's tests and here at runtime, so a corpus that would

fail the bootstrap fails the component's tests first.

node.signature: async fn a_data_steward_holds_the_seat_their_title_grants()
node.doc:
A data steward holds a seat, and the directory says so.



`roles.json` granted `data_steward` nothing until 2026-09-23, which

made the two `data-steward` personas decorative: Cedar permitted them

to approve a publication — `CatalogApprovalGroupMapping` maps the role

to `catalog-data-stewards`, which they carry — and the directory had

no seat to attribute the approval to. Nothing noticed, because the

approval path asked Cedar and not the directory.



Both halves are asked now, so this asserts both answers for a steward:

the policy permits the action, and the seat resolves.



Against a migrated workspace, as its neighbour, with the people

directory loaded.

node.name: same_asset_clone_source
node.signature: async fn same_asset_clone_source( db: &(impl MetadataOperatorRepos + ?Sized), asset: &ConnectorAsset, derivation: &ConnectorDerivation, store_instance: &str, proposed_path: Option<&str>, profile: &SourceProfile, ) -> Result<Option<uuid::Uuid>>
node.doc:
The steward a Unity Catalog owner yields, with the resolution behind it.



A steward is a party the people directory knows. The Unity Catalog owner

is a Databricks principal ("System user" on the sample catalog), so it

becomes the steward only when the directory resolves it; it always stays

on the entry as the owner and in the authorization snapshot, where an

external principal belongs.

The physical side of the asset (RFD-q10sm0wq): the table as a

primary binding in its catalog and schema of the one Unity Catalog store

the sync knows. The entry's `file_path` keeps carrying the same locator

until the readers move to bindings.

The source asset a clone is another binding of, when the default reading

applies (RFD-q10sm0wq d11): the source is bound in this catalog, both

containers resolve to the same default-home taxonomy path, the columns

(name and type) are unchanged, and the clone has not already been

catalogued as its own asset. `None` means the clone is a derived asset.

Runs one pass over an Iceberg REST catalog.



Environment:

- `CAUSEWAY_ICEBERG_REST_URI` (required): the catalog's base URI.

- `CAUSEWAY_ICEBERG_REST_WAREHOUSE`: the warehouse to scope to.

Environment:

- `CAUSEWAY_POSTGRES_SOURCE_INSTANCE`: the store instance label bindings

carry (default `causeway-db`).

- `CAUSEWAY_POSTGRES_SOURCE_SCHEMAS`: comma-separated schemas to read

(default: every non-system schema of the connected database).

- A different database to read is the secret

`[secrets.postgres-source-dsn]` of the topology: a mounted file, with

`CAUSEWAY_POSTGRES_SOURCE_DSN` as its fallback in `local` only. With

neither, the sync reads the operator context's own database.

- The programmatic access token (required) is the secret

`[secrets.snowflake-token]` of the topology: a mounted file, with

`CAUSEWAY_SNOWFLAKE_TOKEN` as its fallback in `local` only.

- `CAUSEWAY_SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`: the warehouse statements run on.

- `CAUSEWAY_SNOWFLAKE_ROLE`: the role statements run as.

- `CAUSEWAY_SNOWFLAKE_DATABASES`: comma-separated databases to read

(default: every database the role sees, less Snowflake's own and the

personal ones).

- `CAUSEWAY_SNOWFLAKE_INSTANCE`: the store instance label bindings

carry (default: the account identifier).



# Errors



Returns an error when the configuration, the account, or the catalog

writes fail.

node.name: discharged_obligations
node.signature: async fn discharged_obligations( &self, entity_id: uuid::Uuid, now: DateTime<Utc>, ) -> Result<Vec<Obligation>>
node.doc:
Loads the obligations discharged by grants in force for one subject.



Reads the approval ledger's projection through the catalog port —

one definition of "active grant" — and reconstructs the exact

`RequireApproval` obligations those grants satisfy. The match is

structural: a grant discharges only the obligation demanding the

same approval kind *and* the same approver role, so a grant recorded

under the wrong role discharges nothing. Grants whose fields do not

parse into the policy vocabulary are skipped with a warning; a grant

the scanner cannot read must never silently discharge a duty.

Routed through the metadata component's active-claims port so

"active" keeps one definition; payloads that do not parse are

skipped with a warning rather than failing the scan row — a claim

the scanner cannot read must not make the asset invisible to every

other policy.

node.name: enqueue_schema_sniff
node.signature: pub async fn enqueue_schema_sniff( db: &(impl MetadataOperatorRepos + ?Sized), entity: &EntityRecord, reason: &str, ) -> Result<()>
node.doc:
Enqueue a schema-sniff request for `entity`. Called after an

ingest path writes a `catalog_assets` row whose `file_path`

points at a sniffable object and whose `columns` are still empty.



Idempotent on `entity_id` — re-enqueueing refreshes the row selected

by the queue's stable idempotency key, clears its previous error, and

makes it immediately claimable. Scheduling also revokes prior source

evidence and moves the current entry to pending before work becomes

visible. A loader, scanner, or object-event consumer therefore cannot

leave stale metadata published while a changed object awaits inspection.

Runs the interpretation stage and records what it produced.



Returns nothing and propagates nothing, deliberately. An interpretation

is enrichment: the format metadata the catalog needs has already been

committed by the time this runs, so a failure here must degrade the

catalog rather than fail a sniff that succeeded. Errors are recorded

against the interpreter, which is what an operator chasing a missing

interpretation needs to find — not a thousand quarantined assets.

registry an operator reads — which is the claim the whole

programme makes and the only one no single slice could prove.

node.doc:
Ensures every glossary term is a metadata entity of the same id.



A claim names its subject through `entities`, and term governance is

a claim on the term (RFD-pbs8n4kn determination 2), so a term must

exist in the spine before anything can be decided about it. The

entity takes the term's registry id, the kind `glossary_term`, the

term key as canonical key, and the URN `urn:causeway:glossary-term:

<key>`; the registration pass that follows then aliases it like any

other entity. Idempotent: an existing entity keeps its id and gains

only a refreshed display name.

node.name: reconcile_sniffs
node.signature: pub async fn reconcile_sniffs(args: ReconcileSniffsArgs) -> Result<SniffReconciliation>
node.doc:
Re-arm a schema sniff for every already-projected entry with a

readable object behind it.



The catalog's stored metadata is only ever as good as the probe that

wrote it. When a probe starts reporting something it did not report

before — a container format where it used to record only a codec —

existing rows keep the older, thinner answer until the object is read

again. Nothing re-reads it on its own: a sniff is scheduled when an

object arrives or changes, and neither happened here. This is the

operator-driven pass that closes that gap.



Entries are skipped rather than failed when they have no concrete

locator: a templated path such as `s3://bucket/{ticker}/{id}` names a

family of objects, so there is nothing to read.



# Errors



Fails if the projection cannot be paged. An entry whose enqueue fails

is counted and logged rather than aborting the pass, because a

half-finished reconcile is more useful than none and the pass is safe

to re-run.
